purpose: Finish the degree-three Gallai-tree side of the max-degree-four 3-colour frontier more sharply. For a retained degree-three component H that is a Gallai tree, characterize exactly when a fixed colouring of the degree-four boundary fails to extend across H. In the 3-colour palette, the classical bad supervalent-list structure collapses to one 3-state label per block and deterministic leaf-to-root propagation. Hence the non-extension relation can be compiled in polynomial time to a conjunction of affine GF(3) equalities/disequalities; the extension relation is one polynomial-size disjunction of affine linear literals. No exponential boundary-colouring table is needed.

source_fact.theorem: For a connected graph with a supervalent list assignment |L(v)|>=d(v), non-list-colourability forces equality |L(v)|=d(v), Gallai-tree block structure, and a decomposition of each vertex list as a union of block palettes L_B with |L_B|=chi(B)-1. This is the Borodin--Erdos--Rubin--Taylor degree-choosability structure in its bad-list form.
sources: Kostochka--Stiebitz--Wirth / Thomassen descriptions of bad degree-list assignments on Gallai trees.
Modern supervalent formulation: if no L-colouring exists then every list is tight and L(v)=union_{B contains v} L_B with |L_B|=chi(B)-1.

input_regime.ambient: Simple graph G of maximum degree at most four after exhaustive degree<=2 peeling and v6.4 deletion of non-Gallai components of the current degree-three layer.
input_regime.component: H is one connected component of the induced subgraph on vertices of current degree three, and H is a Gallai tree.
input_regime.boundary: Every neighbour of H outside H has current degree four. Fix a proper colouring phi of G-V(H) by colours GF(3)={0,1,2}.
input_regime.available_list: For v in H, L_phi(v)=GF(3) minus the set of colours used by neighbours of v outside H. Since deg_G(v)=3, |L_phi(v)|>=d_H(v).

three_colour_block_palettes.K2_block: chi(K2)-1=1, so its bad-list block palette is one colour sigma_B in GF(3).
three_colour_block_palettes.odd_cycle_or_K3_block: chi(B)-1=2, so its palette is GF(3)\{mu_B} for one missing colour mu_B.
three_colour_block_palettes.K4: A K4 block can occur only as a standalone degree-three component; it is an immediate non-3-colourable terminal and is rejected before boundary compilation.
three_colour_block_palettes.subcubic_shape: Apart from standalone K4, cycle/clique blocks contribute internal degree two at each non-cut vertex and can meet the rest of H only through K2 blocks, because two cyclic blocks sharing a cut vertex would give degree at least four inside H.

local_bad_extension_rules.isolated_vertex: If H is one isolated degree-three vertex with three outside neighbours a,b,c, extension fails exactly when phi(a),phi(b),phi(c) are all distinct.
local_bad_extension_rules.K2_leaf: If a non-cut endpoint v of K2 block B has two outside neighbours a,b, badness requires ALLDIFF(phi(a),phi(b),sigma_B). Thus phi(a)!=phi(b) and sigma_B=-(phi(a)+phi(b)) in GF(3).
local_bad_extension_rules.odd_leaf_noncut: If v is a non-cut vertex of odd-cycle/K3 block B, it has one outside neighbour a and badness requires phi(a)=mu_B. Hence all outside neighbours attached to non-cut vertices of one such block must have the same colour mu_B.
local_bad_extension_rules.two_K2_cut: At a cut vertex incident with two K2 blocks B1,B2 and one outside neighbour a, badness is ALLDIFF(sigma_B1,sigma_B2,phi(a)); if one block label and phi(a) are known and distinct, the other label is their unique third colour.
local_bad_extension_rules.three_K2_cut: At a cut vertex incident with three K2 blocks, badness is ALLDIFF(sigma_B1,sigma_B2,sigma_B3).
local_bad_extension_rules.cycle_plus_K2_cut: At a cut vertex incident with an odd-cycle/K3 block B and a K2 block E, there is no outside neighbour and badness requires sigma_E=mu_B.
local_bad_extension_rules.alldiff_linearization: Over GF(3), ALLDIFF(a,b,c) is equivalent to a+b+c=0 together with a!=b. Once any two distinct values are known, the third is uniquely -(a+b).

deterministic_propagation_theorem.name: BAD_GALLAI_BOUNDARY_LABELS_PROPAGATE_WITHOUT_BRANCHING
deterministic_propagation_theorem.statement: For every connected non-K4 Gallai component H and fixed boundary colouring phi, there is at most one assignment of block labels {sigma_B,mu_B} satisfying all bad-list rules. It is found, or disproved, by a leaf-to-root traversal of the block-cut tree.
proof: A leaf K2 block has a non-cut endpoint with two outside neighbours, so its sigma label is uniquely the third colour when those two colours are distinct; otherwise no bad certificate exists.
A leaf odd-cycle/K3 block has non-cut vertices with outside neighbours; all such boundary colours must agree and uniquely determine mu_B.

After a leaf block is labelled, remove it conceptually. At the incident cut vertex the local rule uniquely determines the parent K2 label: equality for cycle-plus-K2, or the unique third colour for a two/three-K2 junction. If a required equality/disequality fails, no bad certificate exists.
Induct on the block-cut tree until the root. The final root condition is only an equality/ALLDIFF check, so no choice is introduced anywhere.
deterministic_propagation_theorem.runtime: Linear in |V(H)|+|E(H)| after block decomposition; all arithmetic is over GF(3).

affine_compilation.symbolic_labels: Run the same leaf-to-root traversal symbolically. A K2 leaf label is -(a+b); an odd block label is one boundary colour subject to equality of the other boundary colours; every internal third-colour step is another negated sum. Therefore every propagated block label is an affine GF(3) linear form in boundary colour variables.
affine_compilation.side_conditions: Every propagation check becomes either equality of two affine forms or disequality of two affine forms. The number of such conditions is O(|H|), and every form can be stored with O(|boundary(H)|) coefficients, hence polynomial total bit size.
affine_compilation.bad_relation: BAD_H(phi) is exactly a conjunction of O(|H|) affine equalities/disequalities over boundary vertex colours.
affine_compilation.extension_relation: EXTEND_H(phi) is NOT BAD_H(phi), hence one disjunction of the negated affine literals. Over GF(3), a literal L!=0 may be written as (L=1 OR L=2), so EXTEND_H has a polynomial-size Res(GF3)-style linear-clause representation.
affine_compilation.elimination: Delete V(H) and attach the compiled boundary linear clause. A colouring of the remaining graph satisfies that clause iff it extends to a proper 3-colouring of H. Reconstruction reruns the deterministic block propagation/list-colouring procedure.

positive: Completes the v6.4 directive on the Gallai-tree side without an exponential table of boundary colourings.
All degree-three Gallai components can be removed from the graph and replaced by polynomial-size affine GF(3) boundary constraints.
The compilation is functional: no hidden branching over block states and no exponential auxiliary-state product.
Odd-cycle/K3 blocks of arbitrary length collapse to one missing-colour state before symbolic elimination.
firewall: This is not a universal 3-COLOR solver. Pure 4-regular instances have no degree-three layer, so the compilation is silent on the known NP-hard 4-regular Hamiltonian source.
The residual problem is a degree-four core coupled to polynomial-size GF(3) linear clauses/disequalities. Tractability of that hybrid system is not proved.
Do not expand the linear clause into all boundary colourings.

next_target.name: E8_DEG4_CORE_PLUS_GF3_LINEAR_CLAUSES_CONTRACTION_V6_6
next_target.directive: Run v5.0 and v6.4-v6.5 first, thereby deleting all degree<=3 structure. Attack the remaining degree-four core together with the compiled GF(3) linear boundary clauses. Seek a polynomial contraction or exact minimax invariant that also makes progress on the pure 4-regular Hamiltonian source, where no boundary clauses are generated. Mandatory controls include K5, fixed-C4-complement Hamiltonian hard instances, and mixed degree-3/4 graphs whose Gallai components compile to long affine literals.
success_obligations: deterministic polynomial construction and solve time
no assignment enumeration or exponential boundary table
must not rely on the presence of degree-three vertices
